what: The battle effects recipe: every number an explosion, smoke, fire, tracer, muzzle flash and dust needs, for the preview clips and for the 3D game. The 3D game should read this file, not copy its numbers into code, so the effects can be tuned without a code change (as the sound mix's mix.json).
made: 2026-11-18, the effects artist, from the art director's sheet art-director/explosions/explosions-look.md (15:43Z), the sound mix sound/mix/mix.json and the tracer rule in tools/battle-models/airshow.py
units: metres, seconds, degrees. Frames are at 30 a second. Colours in [r, g, b] 0 to 255 are what the FINISHED picture should measure (the art director measures pixels), not shader inputs.

rulings.brian: 2026-11-18 15:39Z: 'i want the explosions to be very dramatic and life like... mimic this look and feel as much as possible'; 15:40Z: 'i love how it makes me feel like im in it and watching a movie at the same time'
rulings.own_design: The feeling only. Every effect, texture, sound and camera move is our own; nothing copied from any game (ruling 217, game-direction).
rulings.gore: None: no bodies torn apart (art director's default; Brian may rule otherwise).

burst._how: A high-explosive shell, mortar bomb, grenade or bomb landing on ground. Times are seconds after it lands (frame 0). Sizes scale by sizes.<kind>.scale (1 = 105 mm); the crown's height, crater, linger and shake come straight from the sizes table. On land the EARTH is the star: mostly thrown soil and smoke, almost no fire.

incoming._note: Played only where a real recording exists (mix.json impacts.incoming). Mortars a shorter flutter; tank and anti-tank guns none.

flash._ragged: Art director 19:57Z on build 1748's frames, where the flash was an even orange star, 202,124,6, darker than pale ground (214,196,166): a shell's flash follows the gun flashes' rule. With tongues here it is ragged and new every round: that many tongues of unequal length thrown mostly up and out as the dirt is, the longest reach_m (times the size's root scale), bright at the root and red-orange at the end; licks flung low; a lumpy orange body with a second lump to one side; a yellow inside it written yellow_over times white (lands 250,216,82, luma 214: over pale ground's 198, blue under 110); and a heart heart_share of the flash's width written over times white (lands 253,248,226). It lasts life_s, about two frames, shrinking and dense: the tongues stand among the first dirt, the body, yellow and heart shine through it. Art director 20:12Z: every edge fades out over feather_m (2 to 3 pixels from the battle eye) and no piece is one flat colour. Colours are WRITTEN values (picture._how). Without tongues: the old seven-pointed star in core_colour.
flash._soft: Art director 06:08Z 20 November on build 1758's frames. From 18 m feather_m is about one pixel and the tongues read as cut paper: every feathered edge now fades over at least feather_px pixels on the screen, whatever the distance. And in the game the tongues read as one flat orange (median green over red 0.50): each tongue's root is now yellow-orange (root_yellow of the way from orange to yellow; it lands about 243,202,63, green over red 0.8) from the body out to root_reach of what shows of the tongue, then turns orange and reddens to its tip (in the preview the flames' green over red runs 0.37 to 0.84, median 0.53 to 0.70). Neither key: as before.
flash._melt: Art director 08:03Z 20 November on build 1762's frames from 18 m: the root showed as a flat yellow petal with a firm line round it inside each orange tongue, and the flash read as a flower. With root_melt each tongue is drawn from the point where it leaves the body (root_from of what the body hides of it): orange there, running evenly out to the red-orange of its edge. Its root is the tongue's own shape laid over it, outline for outline, yellow and whole at that same point and thinning evenly to nothing at the tongue's rim, half gone root_melt of the way out and turning orange as it thins. So the yellow melts into the orange along the tongue and across it with no line anywhere, the hottest yellow runs down the centre line, and the edges are orange to red-orange. Heart, body, sizes, timing and dice are as they were. No root_melt: build 1762's root.

light._rule: a real light on the men, vehicles and ground within the radius; lifts the lower third of the frame 1.1 to 1.3x, never a white-out; checked by measuring the frame against the one before
light._passed: The fortifications 105 mm burst passed 17:11Z with its lamp 16 m up: ground lifted 1.24x at 3 m, 1.19x at 10 m, 1.12x at 15 m, a tank's side 1.10x at 28 m, gone by frame 3. Height scales by the square root of the size's scale. (Its second, low lamp that lit only the men and the tank is left out: the game has two lamps for all the flashes.)

flash._dusk: At dusk and night the flash lights the young smoke from inside for 3 or 4 frames: the most cinematic moment we have.
flash._core: Not a pale heart: yellow, blue channel under 110 (the fortifications burst passed 17:11Z with the pale heart at frame 0 left for the kit to fix).

ember._what: What the flash leaves low in the earth: a dull orange glow no wider than 'share' of the flash, dying to dark ('to') over life_s (art director 19:58Z 21 November: at most a third of the flash's width, 0.15 to 0.3 s).

skirt._shade: how strongly the skirt is lit on top and shadowed at its foot (1 is every other puff), so it shows its height (art director 17:09Z)
skirt._mend_1931: Art director 19:31Z: the skirt must be one low continuous haze, never puffs. Its pieces are now drawn as low flattened balls seen from where the eye is (a low wall from the side, the whole round they cover from above, where they used to be thin upright cards that read as separate dabs), larger, more of them, softer and fainter, so they run together.
skirt._budget: Fewer, larger pieces since they cover their whole round from above (19:45Z): 130 a 105 where 250 overflowed the room in a battery's salvo (the pre-check's count).
skirt._mend_0319: Art director 03:13Z (Brian's battle clips): from a low eye the skirt was a big flat beige pancake that veiled the crown's foot. Cut to reach 9 m, alpha 0.22 to 0.3; its rim broken into lobes (5 to 7, of uneven reach, never less than lobe_least of the reach between them); its outer feather share of the reach fading to a sixth, each piece soft from its middle out (heart 0); its top under most_high_m (times the square root of scale), rising only rise_mps as it hazes. Pass: no visible rim from a 1.7 m eye.

shock_ring.grass: flattens outward, springs back over 0.6 s
shock_ring._note: One continuous low skirt in the ground's own dust colour, racing out and thinning (art director 16:31Z), with height and a soft billowing top, settling to a low haze by frame 30 (16:53Z). Neighbours overlap by about half; each puff is an upright card, long along the ring, so its foot never cuts into the ground.
shock_ring._why_085: the skirt's tops face the sun and the ground is seen edge-on, so the ground's own dust drawn at full brightness reads paler than the ground; 0.85 matches it
shock_ring._ground_skirt: Art director 19:58Z 21 November: a low ring of dust rolls outward along the ground to 1.5 times the cloud's width over 1 to 2 s, stays low, and hangs with the cloud. of_cloud: the skirt's width across as that many times the size's cloud_m (the metres below are for a reach of roll_ref_m, a 105's, and go by the reach). skirt.hangs: it stays as long as the cloud, going as the cloud goes by the size's own linger times, never climbing; it keeps hang_keep times the cloud's share of its pieces, and widens and spreads hang_wide and hang_spread as much as the cloud's puffs do.

body._note: A dense dark mound of earth and dust at the crown's foot from frame 4, so the hit has weight; it slumps into the smoke.

foot_glow._art_director: 22:24Z (dusk salvo sheet): a flash's edge stays at about 180,75,35 or a warmer grey, never fully saturated; was 184,100,3. It dies to a warm grey ember (66,36,22), not a pure red.

crown.then: collapses into the smoke and rains back as a veil
crown._note: A wide torn fan (about 100 degrees) thrown outward from the point (art director 16:31Z and 16:53Z): a few heavy dark jets, very uneven in length and width, overlapping and bunched, never spaced like fingers; the gaps filled with lighter dust (fill_jets) so the silhouette is one torn fan; each heavy jet thinnest and torn at its tip, drawn to a point (tip_point), never rounded, with clods flying on beyond it (tip_clod_speed); a dense dark body at the foot from frame 4. Jet thickness is a share of the crown's height (jet_foot_r, jet_tip_r) and puffs are stepped along a jet by their own length (overlap), so a bomb's jets do not bead.
crown.azimuth: random round the compass, never evenly spaced: jets overlap and bunch
crown._edges: edge_jitter: how far each puff along a jet strays sideways, as a share of the jet's width; lump_chance: how many puffs are lumps half again or twice as wide. Ragged, clumpy sides, never smooth blades or leaves (art director 17:09Z).
crown._edge_rough: Each jet puff's outline is lumpy by this share (fill jets 0.6 of it), so a jet's sides are clumpy, never a smooth blade, with no more puffs.
crown._root: Art director 19:43Z: earth flying up is heavy at the root and thins only near the tip, with side edges broken as the clods are. Up to root_solid of a heavy jet's length its puffs are denser, and at each step a dense lumpy clump bulges out of its side (side_clumps is the chance).
crown._tips_1943: Art director 19:43Z: jet sides read as glass shards or blades. The cause was each big heavy piece's wide see-through band (solid only to half its radius, then thinning to a hard rim), drawn with straight sides between the ring's points. Now a heavy piece is solid out to heavy_inner of its radius (heavy_heart) and fades in a thin soft edge with no rim, so its lumpy outline shows and nothing is glassy. The root stays dense and dark up to root_solid with clumps bulging from its sides (side_clumps); the tip is torn into smaller, rougher, scattered pieces (tip_grain, tip_rough, tip_inner), drawn out and pointed less (tip_stretch 1.2, tip_point 0.45). The lighter dust between the jets is scattered wider, lumpy and soft, never pointed (fill_scatter, fill_rough, fill_stretch).
crown._heavy_jets_0319: Art director 03:13Z (Brian's battle clips): 24 to 40 thin dark spiky jets in place of 5 to 8 heavy ones. The shells keep 3 to 5 heavy jets for the mass and add the spikes (burst.crown.spikes); the bombs keep their own passed fan (sizes.<bomb>.crown).

spikes._how: Thin dark rays of earth among the heavy jets: count of them (halved past burst.debris.shower.halve_past puffs), each a few lumps (pieces) along its length with small gaps (each lump lump_share of its place), edges broken by rough (foot to tip), drawn to a point, reaching reach times the crown's height, leaning lean times half the fan, thick times the jet's foot and tip radius, the heavy colour times shade, alpha falling to tip_alpha at the tip, a lump of tip_clod_m (times the square root of scale) riding each tip. The debris shower streams along them too. droop: the outer lumps fall faster (gravity up to 1 + droop at the tip), so the tip bends down after about 0.3 s. longest_of_median: no spike longer than this times the middle one (a long lone blade reads as a stick). stretch_most: no lump drawn longer than this times its width. Art director 03:28Z.

crown._streaks: Art director 03:27Z 22 November: at half a second the crown was 'a few broad flat wedges with straight edges... cardboard slabs. Keep the mass, but make it more, narrower streaks with soft tips that fall back by about 1.5 s.' So more heavy jets, each thinner (heavy_jets, heavy_thick); heavy_stretch: a heavy jet's pieces drawn that long for their width and stepped as far apart, so a thin jet is a streak of few pieces; heavy_swell: they widen that much over their lives and no more; heavy_droop: a piece falls faster the further up its jet (gravity up to 1 + heavy_droop at the tip), so the tips come back down; tip_life_s: how long the piece at the very tip lasts, the root's as ever; tip_heart, tip_alpha, tip_inner: a soft end. A size may have its own of each. The thin jets are paid for in pieces: fewer clumps on a jet's side, one or two clods off each tip, fewer spikes of fewer lumps, fewer fill jets and foot lumps, so a 105 holds about as many pieces as before (1,104 against 1,037 at most, and a barrage holds fewer).

foot._how: Art director 03:13Z, from Brian's battle clips: close-hit black is 29% of the burst in the clips and 0.8% in ours; the burst itself has to carry the black, no grade can. A dense mass of near-black lumps at the crown's base (and the crown's body near-black with it): count lumps (times the square root of scale, at least 0.7), out to width and up to height times the crown's height, each lump_r times the crown's height, the heavy colour times shade (near black), lit on top and dark below by light, lumpy by rough, living life_s and settling toward the smoke's colour mixed with settle_dust of the dust, settle of the way by its end, so near-black for 0.3 to 1.0 s, then brown-grey. Not on water. Pass: at 0.4 s on earth, at least 15% of the burst box under luma 60. The earth veil over the foot is the dust mixed veil_dark toward the heavy colour, and the smoke puffs in the lower smoke_band of the cloud start smoke_dark as bright, settling to the cloud's own colour by smoke_settle_s. The dust between the jets is the heavy colour mixed with fill_dust of its usual dust share, settling the same way.

clods._passed: With the clods thrown from the jets' tips, about 130 in all for a 105, landing 0.9 to 3.1 s after the flash, the big ones bouncing once (the fortifications burst, passed 17:11Z).
clods._chunk: Irregular chunks, never smooth beans (art director 19:36Z): each clod has its own lumpy outline (rough), tumbles as it flies, and has a lit face toward the sun and a dark one away (shade).

lens._rule: on a hit close to the camera a few clods and a veil of grit cross the foreground: what puts the player in the hole

debris._note: True gravity sells weight: a clod thrown 10 m up comes down about 2.8 s later.

shower._why: Brian's battle video (11-19): what makes a hit read as violent is a dense spray of dark lumps flung higher than the crown and twice as wide, raining back for one to three seconds. Ours threw a few small clods low. The shower: count lumps for a 105 (times the ground's shower share, default its clods share, and the shell's size squared up to most_k2), thrown up_mps and out_mps (both times the fourth root of the shell's scale, so a 105 tops out at 2 to 13 m and lands 1.2 to 3.3 s later), radius r_m (times the square root of scale; small_skew keeps most small), darkened by shade (backlit undersides), resting rest_s on the ground, a landing puff only from landing_puff_r_m. Water throws none. along_jets of them stream along the crown's jets (each within jet_spread of its way, at jet_speed times the speed that carries a lump to that jet's tip, so some fall short inside it and some fly on past), the rest flung every way at up_mps and out_mps.
shower._halve: Art director 03:13Z: with more than halve_past puffs live when a shell lands, it throws half the shower and half the spikes.

debris._dust_trails: Art director 19:58Z 21 November: dark clods tumble and fall back within 2 to 3 s (sizes.<size>.clods_back_s), a few trailing thin dust: dust_trails of the clods over dust_trail_from_m in radius (for a 105; by the size) shed a thin line of dust along their flight.

smoke.build: many small puffs, never a few big balls; volumes in the preview renders
smoke.merge: neighbours overlap; sizes vary 1 to 3 times; soft rims, no firm cores: never separate round balls like grapes (art director 16:53Z)
smoke._top: Warm brown near the ground, charcoal grey toward the top: brown all the way up reads as dust (art director 19:36Z). Each puff mixes toward colour_top by its height in the cloud, up to top_share.
smoke._cloud: Art director 19:43Z: the cloud's sunward side about 15 to 20 levels lighter than its shadow side, and its top broken into 3 to 5 lumps, not one smooth dome. cloud_shade lights or shadows each puff by where it sits in its cloud (as game.shade_lit and shade_dark), fully beyond cloud_r of the crown's height from the cloud's leaning middle; top_lobes gathers the upper puffs into a few lumps. Preview, 105 on earth at frame 40, sun from the side: the sunward third about 15 levels lighter than the shadow third once the cloud's own thinner downwind side is taken off (about 13 by halves).

scar.overlap: craters overlap where hits overlap: a barrage ploughs a green field

bulk._what: A burst with bulk (Brian, 18:30Z 21 November: 'the explosions should be bigger and more more realistic'; the art director's ruling of 19:58Z, art-director/explosions/smoke-burst-fire-ruling-r2.md): more bulk, a denser core and a longer hang, never a ball of soft smoke lifting off the ground. Where a size has cloud_m, its cloud is a column of the ground's own dark earth standing on the hit, many puffs at every height, hiding what is behind it through its first two seconds, in lighter grey-brown smoke and dust that is cloud_m across at the ground by about two seconds. It climbs from its foot and stays on the ground. Remove this row, or a size's cloud_m, and that cloud is the old one.
bulk._how: column: 'puffs' of them (more for a bigger burst), in a stack 'wide' of cloud_m across at the ground and top_wide of that at its top, 'tall' of the crown high; each puff_r of cloud_m in radius, as thick as 'alpha', its outline 'rough'; the top stands by climb_s and rises on at rise_mps, the foot not at all; 'soil' and 'shade' its colour between the ground's heavy earth and its soil, going 'settle' of the way to the settled brown-grey over life_s. fringe: 'puffs' of lighter smoke, 'tall' of the crown high, 'taper' narrower at its top than at the ground, rolling out to its place over roll_s.

throw._what: A shell's thrown earth at its flash (art director 03:27Z 22 November, on the bigger bursts: 'the throw at the flash is near black... a black comic-book splat with an orange dot. Make it dark earth brown with the faces toward the flash lit warm, floor about 15'). lighter and body: the jets, the spikes, the body and the foot are made lighter than the ground's heavy earth has them, until its brightest channel is the written value body (75 lands about 50), never more than lighter times: so they have a lit side and a shaded one above the floor, and sand or rubble, light already, stay as they are. mottle: each piece that share lighter or darker than the next, by its own lump seed, so a jet is streaked earth and never one flat fill. floor: no point of the jets, the spikes, the body, the foot or the column of earth is drawn darker than this, in the hour's light. flash_lit: how far the earth nearest the flash goes toward flash_colour on its side toward the flash as it goes off, dying to nothing over flash_lit_s; half as much flash_lit_reach of the flash's own width from it. A piece the eye sees from the flash's side is lit all over, one standing in front of it only on its edge. Not on water. Both colours are written values, aimed through the game's curve (picture._how): the floor lands about 40,33,26, 16 on the art director's scale of 100; flash_colour lands about 180,117,58. Remove the row and the throw is as it was.

sizes._how: Rough figures, already about 1.3 times real so they read at the battle camera (art director). Check in the scene against a known-size fitting: a man, 1.75 m. scale is for the puff and clod counts and sizes; shake is camera shake within shake_within_m.

light._proposed: the effects artist 16:55Z, for the field battle's 'light' shells (37 to 57 mm); the art director to confirm

crown._note: Art director 20:00Z: a bomb's crown at frame 8 read as rabbit ears, two tall thin jets alone in a V. A bomb throws 5 to 9 heavy jets spaced round the compass (spread_even: each nudged by up to that share of a gap), so the fan shows from every side; the second tallest is clearly shorter than the tallest (second_reach, and heavy_lean at most 0.8 of the half fan, so it is at least a quarter shorter however it leans); at least three more reach half the tallest one's height or over (mid_jets, mid_reach); the rest are short (heavy_reach) and lean further out (short_lean), so the fan spans about 100 degrees at its foot. A dense dark body about a third of the crown's height stands at the root, so the jets rise out of a mass and never stand on the skirt like stalks. Height stays at the size's crown_m.
crown._pieces: Art director 20:05Z: at bomb size the big pieces showed flat faces with straight edges, like a dark crystal cluster. A piece's outline has the ring's few points however big it is, so a bomb's jets are built of more pieces no bigger than piece_max_m (radius when thrown), scattered across each jet's width, and the body's pieces are lumpy (body.rough) with soft edges (body.rim 0).

torpedo._what: a torpedo against a ship's side (the scene passes this size for it; a kit without the row draws a field gun's burst, so pass it only with this recipe). On water: the tallest, narrowest column, over the mast, dark for its lower third.

churn._what: white water round a ship that is settling, going down or rolling over (the scene passes this size for it, on water only): no explosion, so quiet 1, no flash and no jolt. A low boil several times wider than it is tall (art director 22:03Z: the first was a white hedgehog mound): domes of pale water heaving up a few metres and sinking back, no two at the same moment, froth breaking round the foot of each, darker water between them, a burst of spray here and there as air vents, and a wide patch of foam that lasts. dome_in_s: each dome's water comes up out of the sea over that long, never all at once (the pre-check measured the patch's ink rising a sixth in one frame as a dome was born; art director 23:19Z: ease it in over about 0.3 s).

grounds._how: The ground under the hit decides the look. thrown is the crown's colour against the ground's own (or a fixed colour where given); smoke tints the cloud. The 3D field's ground kinds (open, field, woods, rough, marsh, water, road, bridge, buildings, rock, bunker, works, blown) map to these by ground_of.

sand.extra: pale, tall, slow dust cloud; glows when backlit
sand.core: darker damp sand in the heavy jets, inside the pale slow column, so it reads as a hit
sand._shower: A shell in sand still throws stones and damp lumps high (the video's beach): shower 0.8, though its clods share stays 0.15.

snow.crater: a black star on white with a grey-brown spatter ring
snow.extra: white snow thrown up first, dark earth under it
snow._mend_1931: Art director 19:31Z on the first in-game frames: the snow crown was smooth pure-white blades like a paper flower, ringed by cotton puffs. Now broken and granular (grain: its pieces half the size, twice as many, soft-edged, not drawn out), off-white (about 188,193,201 in shade; each grain its own shade) with dark earth showing in the jets (first_share: a third of the pieces snow at the jet's foot, four fifths at its tip).

mud.clod_kind: wet clumps that splash, not spray
mud.crater: black-brown spatter, water shining in it
mud.ground_shine: matt: wet earth, not a glaze

town.extra: grey-white masonry dust is the cloud's main colour and hangs in the street
town._shower: Masonry lumps and tiles in the shower, in the town's clod colour: shower 0.8, though town throws no earth clods.

woods.tree_burst: the trunk left torn and pale where it split

water.rule: the splash column already passed: rises in 2 frames, dark foot ring, never cotton wool
water._spout: Brian's battle video (11-19): a water spout is white spray that falls back fast and leaves a thin mist, not a cloud. The smoke's top mixes toward smoke_top (pale grey: burst.smoke.colour_top is charcoal, for earth), its puffs are smoke_alpha as solid, the mist clears in about a third of the time (haze_lingers), and nothing smoulders. Art director 03:28Z: the mist at 1.6 s was a round white ball; the wind draws each puff out smoke_stretch times downwind (and carries some further than others), and it thins to half by smoke_half_by_s.

spout._how: A hit in the sea (art director 17:54Z 20 November, from build 1778: the columns were soft white billows that hung like steam or cotton). With this row a shell, bomb or torpedo in the water throws white water and nothing else: a column up to the size's crown_m in about rise_s (a 50 m one; a small splash sooner), wide of its height at its stalk and crown_wide at its head. Its body stands to three quarters of the height; the top is fingers that rise inside it and bend out of its head (fingers of them, leaning finger_lean_deg at their tips, the tallest to the full height, the next clearly shorter, the rest finger_reach of it), each drawn to a torn point. Streamers of spray leave their heads (streamers a finger) and the column's sides (side_spray): each streamer_pieces pieces thrown one after another out to streamer_out of the column's height, so it is an arc that bends over under its own weight, thicker at its root and breaking into beads at its tip, and is gone before the column's top is down (art director 22:03Z: single streaks were dead-straight hairlines like a firework, and hung over the column like rain). The water goes up as a jet, each piece jet_stretch as long as it is wide (1.9 to 2.8 unless given), and comes down as a curtain, drawn out longer as it falls, the top back on the sea in fall_s. Its lowest base_to is dark wet water (base_colour) that breaks white above, with a low heave of the same round its foot (foot). The side away from the sun is shaded toward shadow by side_shade. A low ring of spray races out over the sea (surge) to foam_reach of the height; foam lies where it stood in a soft mottled patch (foam pieces, foam_alpha, gone in foam_s); a thin mist (mist puffs of mist_alpha, mist_s) goes off down the wind. body: the column's pieces, none bigger than piece_max_m. A small splash is fewer and coarser pieces by its height, and so is a hit far off: so far that a 50 m column would stand under full_px tall in the picture (the scene's window pixels), it has that share of its pieces, never under far_least, each as much bigger. Past halve_past pieces asked for on the screen, a new column is half as many, and with the room four fifths full a quarter. A size may set any of these under sizes.<size>.spout, and domes there: no column at all, but that many low domes of water heaving up and sinking back over the column's width (the churn's). Without this row: the old crown of pale dust and its hanging mist.

by_month.snow: the campaign month and weather say snow
by_month.mud: the autumn and spring thaw (rasputitsa) in the east, and marsh
by_month.sand: North Africa and the desert fields

grounds._paint: paint: the game's unlit colours for each ground, as the finished picture should show them (sRGB 0-255): soil the lighter jets, heavy the dark heavy jets and the body, dust the skirt and veil, clod the lumps, smoke the cloud, first (snow) what is thrown first, splinter (woods) the wood. ring (optional) the dust ring's colour, from the ground it lands on (default dust: art director 03:28Z, earth's ring grey-brown, a touch darker than its dust); foot (optional) the dark foot's colour (default heavy: sand's is grey-black explosive smoke); stone (optional) the shower's lumps (default clod: sand throws dark stones). foot_dust (optional) how much of the ground's dust shows in the dark foot's veil and fill (snow 0: black earth through the white, art director 03:28Z).
grounds._clod_written: Art director 17:08Z (build 1732, where one big clod was taken for a glitch): the game's grade crushes darks (picture._how), so a clod painted 40,33,26 showed as a black hole with no detail. The dark grounds' clod paints are WRITTEN values, aimed through the game's curve (tools/battle-fx/game_curve.py) to show as they were painted: earth 69,62,55 shows as 40,33,26; mud 64,58,52 as 34,28,22; snow 74,69,64 as 48,42,36; woods 80,72,64 as 56,46,36. Clods only: sand's and town's are light enough as they are, and no other dark paint is changed. At about 34 luma they still count toward the burst's black (under 60: burst.foot._how).

fire._how: Only where something burns: fuel, an ammunition load, a fuel dump, a plane, a burning room, a wreck. Never a big orange ball on a ground hit.
fire.heart: yellow, short tongues, blue channel under 110
fire.shape: long, ragged, tapering tongues rooted where it burns; they die by being eaten away, never by thinning
fire.render_note: In the preview renders flame emission stays about (0.16, 0.042, 0.0) at the puff material's strength 7, or the AgX tone curve bleaches it peach whatever its hue (fortifications thread). Measure every flame.
fire.blast_cloud: warm only at its foot, charcoal above

fire._passed: Flame 207, 134, 56 at frame 0 and the crown's foot glow 184, 100, 3 at frame 2, gone by frame 6: both passed in the fortifications 105 mm burst, 17:11Z.
fire._smoke_rest: Art director 18:28Z (build 1746, Pearl Harbor from the air: a wide see-through sheet of smoke beside a burning ship ended along a straight level line). A fire's smoke puff grows to two to four times the fire's width while it climbs only 20 to 30 m, so a 40 m ship fire's puffs, 80 to 160 m in radius, stood half under the sea and the sea cut each along a straight line. smoke_rest: the puff's middle is never lower than this share of its own radius above the ground or sea under it (Bit::Rest), so the cloud stands on the surface. 0 or no key: as before. A small fire's smoke already rides higher than it is wide and does not move.
fire._smoke_foot: Art director 19:57Z (build 1748, Pearl Harbor from the air): the smoke now stands on the sea, but the puffs lying there had paled with age to a sunlit grey bank at the column's foot and read as steam. Smoke is youngest and darkest at the fire. smoke_foot: while a big fire's smoke puff lies on the ground or sea (see smoke_rest) it keeps this dark, after the flames too; written 50, 46, 42 it lands about 18, the oil column's own dark. It takes its own, paler colour only as it rides clear of where it rests, all of it by smoke_foot_clear of its radius. smoke_foot_from_m: how big a fire, from the width where this begins to the width where it is whole; a tank's or a house's fire is under it and smokes as before. No key: as before.

smoke_bank._how: Art director 03:30Z 20 November (build 1750, Pearl Harbor from the air; Akagi in picture 06): the smoke resting on the sea beside a big fire was a smooth, soft dark oval with no lumps and no edge, a stain or a hole in the water. A fire from_m across or more lays its smoke as a bank of the oil column's own kind of lumps (rough, heart, twin_px, its sunward lumps lit toward lit_colour by sun_side), run out down the wind. The bank: its lumps wander wide times the fire's width apart by the far end and it is long times that in length; measured from straight above it comes to 2.2 to 2.9 times as long as it is wide. Each lump is lump_r of the fire's width in radius, is born on the fire every every_s (while it flames, after) and runs down the wind at the pace that takes the longest lived (life_s, for a 40 m fire; a 12 m fire's about half) to the far end. All live through the first short share of that, piling into one dark mass at the fire; fewer and fewer live on (thin: higher, fewer), each solid for hold of its life, so down the wind the bank thins to lumps apart with clear sea between. Most lie on the sea (rise_mps, rest) and keep the fire's dark (smoke_foot), each its own shade; heads of them lift (head_rise_mps) and pale as they ride clear. A young lump is lit only sun_young as much until sun_from of the longest life and in full by sun_by of it (art director 04:06Z: the dark pile at the root, the first third, takes about a tenth of the light and lands near the passed foot, luma about 32 and near neutral, reading by its edge against the sea; the light comes in through the middle so the far lumps keep their lit tops). Every dial is held to a sane span in the code. No such key, or a fire under from_m (a tank, a house): the old smoke, unchanged.

smoke_column._how: A big fire's own column (art director 04:06Z 20 November: a burning ship gets a column of her own, of the oil column's kind but about half its width: black at the root, lumps, leaning down the wind, rising a few hundred metres before it bends flat; the bank lies on the sea beneath it). A plain fire (Burn) from_m across or more that burns from_s seconds or longer sends one up: the oil column's own puffs and pall (the keys below are the oil row's, read the same way, sizes as shares of the fire's width), laid from this row. from_s: a shorter fire sends up none (a crashed aeroplane's 90 seconds lays its bank only). One column to a ship: a fire lit within join_m of a place a standing column rises from joins it; the column then rises from both fires and from between them (eight places at most; a fire that joins after that adds none, so a ship struck again and again keeps her one column), stands on their middle, and is join_wide of her burning length across (the fires' greatest distance apart plus the new fire's width; never wider than a fire join_m across would send up), so a carrier ablaze from end to end sends up one broad column and never three chimneys. most: so many columns stand at once and never more (each is some 95 to 130 puffs that are kept when the screen is full, as an oil column's are); a fire past that lays its bank only, chosen as it is lit and never by the eye. under_oil: none of it is laid while burning oil (OilFire) stands within this share of that oil's reach of one of her fires: the game lights an oil fire 0.6 of her length across on every ship lost, and that oil's column is hers. A column that oil has stood over does not stand again when the oil goes out, and takes no place among the most; a fire lit under burning oil starts none. 0: laid all the same. sun_young, sun_from_s, sun_by_s: a puff has only sun_young of its lit side until sun_from_s seconds old and all of it by sun_by_s, so the column is black at its root and its lit lumps come in higher up (any oil row can ask the same; none asked: as before). After the flames the column thins, greys and comes half as often until the fire ends. No fire.smoke_column.column_life_s key: no column, every fire as before.
smoke_column._tight: A small fire's column held in one piece (art director 15:40Z 20 November on the outcome looks' first cuts: 'at 300 m the ship fire's smoke breaks into a scatter of separate flakes. Each puff should overlap the next at every distance, at least 1.5 times the spacing with a floor in pixels'). A puff's size goes by the fire's width, but the scatter the row's spread of windage and push gives two puffs does not: over a 12 m fire the puffs were a fifth as wide as over a 60 m one and thrown as far apart. tight_m: a fire narrower than this keeps only its share (its width over tight_m) of that spread, so its puffs go nearly one way; at this width or wider nothing is changed (three fires along Akagi make a column 55 m wide: Midway 06 is laid as passed). overlap: under tight_m each puff is at least this many times as wide as the way to the next one, young and old, with what scatter is left. least_px, least_keep: far off a puff of the column is never under this many window pixels across, keeping that share of its ink. Without the keys: as before.

put_out._how: A fire its crew puts out (art director 14:39Z 20 November; BurnOut on a fire lit with a number): 'the smoke turns white, then the fire is gone'. over_s: seconds in which the flames are eaten back from the edges to the seat, lower and in fits, never thinner, when the caller gives none. surge_s: with water (a ship's hoses) white steam surges at the seat that long as it hits (the steam.surge row); with an extinguisher (a tank's crew) a brief pale puff instead. pale_s: by then the smoke has gone from black through grey to grey-white; it thins to a wisp and is gone gone_s after the crew began. The flames shrink steadily, half their height by two fifths of that time, never all gone and back. Where it burned a dull patch (glow, glow_alpha) lies on the seat and small specks flicker over it, embers of them alight at once at first and fewer to the end, embers_s after the last flame (art director 16:41Z: never round red lamps). No such row: BurnOut does nothing.

tongues._how: A burning thing's flames (Burn). Art director 17:54Z 20 November, from build 1778's ships: the fires were rows of pointed orange cones like birthday candles. With this row a fire burns at seats of its own (seats of them, fixed on the skin where it was lit, standing apart round its middle). Each seat throws ragged tongues tall of the fire's width high, each seat its own share of that so no two are the same height, one the tallest and more of them short (a fire over tall_wide_m across is less tall for its width); a tongue is wide of the width at its root, lives life_s and dies by being eaten away from below. A seat's height surges and sinks by pulse several times a second, no two seats together. A tongue leans lean for each metre a second of wind, lean_most at the most, and bends further over toward its tip. forks of them have a thinner tongue out of the same root leaning aside, and tips of them a thin tip above the body, so a flame's top is torn and never one point. Colour (art director 23:19Z: each flame was one flat orange from root to tip): a tongue is body at its root, running out to orange and then to tip, a dull deep red, at its edge and its top, and it reddens as it dies; its thin tip is that red, going darker. Under the tongues each seat keeps a bed that never goes out while the fire burns: a broad yellow foot where the flame leaves the skin, and along it, across the eye's line, two short blunt licks of root, white-yellow, burning root_over past white under the tallest seat and less under the rest (picture.lit_gain), so the heart of the fire is a ragged bright band along its foot and never a disc. foot_soft: the share of a lick, from its root out to its rim, over which it fades away (0.4 without the key; the art director 23:51Z: soften the licks a little so they do not read as cut shapes up close). torn: the chance a step (every_s) of a scrap torn off a tall tongue's top: ragged, blunt, dull red going to the smoke's dark, gone in a quarter of a second within a tongue's height (the first were darts flying across the smoke, which read as sparks). over_smoke: the fire's flames are sorted this share of its width nearer the eye, so its far seats show through its own smoke and are not blacked out by it (from a ship's distance they were). A fire under full_px wide in the picture (the scene's window pixels) burns at that share of its seats, never under seats_least, each as much wider, with as much fewer forks, tips and torn tips; and one under far_px wide stands taller, up to far_tall more, so far off it reads as fire before smoke. As the room fills a fire keeps its bed and its tongues' bodies and loses the forks, tips and torn tips, by degrees from seven tenths full to none at seventeen twentieths. Put out, it is eaten back to its middle, steadily lower and at fewer seats. Without this row: one or two upright cones a step, anywhere on the fire.

shake._how: A short jolt on hits inside sizes.<kind>.shake_within_m, scaled by size and nearness: strength = scale * (1 - distance / within)^2. Hits beyond the radius never shake it. A setting turns shake off.

shake.setting: Options: Camera shake on or off (default on)

depth.far: bursts small, softened and greyed by haze; flashes on the horizon; tall smoke columns standing over the far side of the field

muzzle._how: A gun firing. The flame is a ragged tongue along the bore with licks thrown sideways, under one frame; its lamp lights the gun and its pit, out before the next frame. Then grey-brown smoke rolls out, hangs and drifts. Big guns throw a ring of dust off the ground in front.

mg.smoke: a thin haze over the gun while it fires

tank_gun.case: ejected 0.7 s later (sound only within 40 m)

at_gun._note: fires flat from low down: the dust it throws off the ground in front can hide the gun for a moment, as it really did

mortar.smoke: a short puff up the tube's line

muzzle._day_lamp: By day only rows with day_lamp light the ground (at game.day_lamp_share); tank guns, anti-tank guns, machine guns, rifles and mortars do not (art director 21:16Z).

veil._how: Art director 06:19Z, the desert: a tank or field gun's shot (any row with dust_ring_m; a towed gun's muzzle socket too) raises the ground round the muzzle in a veil spread along the line of fire, rising a metre or two (every other puff a low dense skirt on the ground, dust.vehicles.low_skirt), that hides the gun and its line of sight for hide_s, then thins to haze_alpha and lingers on the wind. by_ground: where it rises (and how thick); the ring itself takes the ground's own paint and grounds.<g>.dust against earth's.
veil._lumps: Art director 18:28Z: the desert veil gets the tank gun's treatment (muzzle.billows), lumps and never upright sheets. lumps: that many times puffs, each a lump lump_r of a sheet's radius across (so several sizes, 0.7 to 2 m for a tank gun) and lump_thick of the veil's thickness (thick ones and thin ones, with gaps), with the billows' firm heart and rough outline, lit as one cloud; every other one a mound lying on the ground, the rest thrown up lump_up_m over it and thinner the higher by lump_pale_up. lump_tuft_share of them thin to haze_alpha by hide_s and linger for life_s as the veil did; the others are gone soon after hide_s. With game.near_eye_fade_m it fades out near the camera. Tried at twice the count and size: a pale wash over the lower frame. 0 or no key: the ten upright sheets as before.

billows._how: Art director 17:52Z on build 1746's test, where a tank gun fired 4 m from two riflemen and its smoke lay over them as one even beige gauze: a heavy gun blinding the men beside it is right, but it must read as dust, not fog. A field gun's shot (a row whose flame_m is 0.5 or more) raises a cloud in three layers, each a scatter of lumps of several sizes and thicknesses with gaps between, never one sheet. low: dense mounds of the ground's own dust resting on the ground under and ahead of the muzzle, over reach of its dust ring (shares of dust_ring_m, behind to ahead) and wide of it to each side, each low_r of the ring across. mid: lumps of dust and smoke (smoke_mix of game.muzzle_smoke) thrown up over them, mid_up_m above the ground, mid_r of the ring across, thinner by pale_up and sooner gone the higher they start. top: the gun's own smoke thrown along the bore from the muzzle and scattered off it at scatter_mps, top_r of the flame's length across (plus 0.2 m); the further it flies and the higher, the thinner. So the cloud is heaviest low and near the muzzle and thins upward, and men behind it come clear from the head down. Each layer is thick for a little under half its life, then thins: mid and low live clear_s, top top_s, so the thick part is gone in 1.5 to 2 s. Of the low mounds, tuft_share settle to haze_alpha by haze_by_s and drift on the wind for tuft_s as tufts. low, mid, top are a tank gun's counts (a wider ring and a longer flame throw more); dust goes by the ground's own (grounds.<g>.dust against earth's). heart, inner: how solid a lump is and how far out (a firm body with a short soft edge shows its lumpy outline, rough); shade: its sunward side lit and far side shadowed. A lump never sinks into the ground: its middle stays its own radius clear of it. Without low, a gun smokes as it did before (17 soft puffs along the bore). The gun's low dust ring (dust_ring_m) and the desert's veil (veil, sand only) are as they were.

dry._how: Art director 06:08Z 20 November on build 1758's west still on sand: half a second after the shot the dry lumps and the gun's smoke wisps were still one soft cloud, and two riflemen 4 m off the line of fire, seen across it, almost vanished. On a ground named in by_ground (its number: how many times the pieces) a heavy gun's blast (a row with dust_ring_m) raises four to six big dense lumps and nothing thin. tall of them stand where the blast strikes the ground hardest, at the muzzle's two flanks and just ahead of it, never behind it: each tall_r of the ring across with two shoulders, about man-high for a tank gun. low of them are heaps of two lobes farther down the line of fire, one to a stretch with clear ground between, each low_r of the ring across, smaller the farther out. The gun's own smoke is puffs dense puffs at the muzzle, puff_r of the flame across, taking smoke_as_dust of the dust's colour. Every piece is alpha thick to inner of its radius with a lumpy outline (rough) and is lit as a thing with form (light: how strongly its sunward side is lit and its far side shadowed): in the preview its lit top lands 1.08 to 1.10 times the ground, its shadow side about two thirds. The heaps are gone by clear_s; the tall ones hold to near_s, thinning, the cloud that gives the gun away. Colour: the ground under the muzzle as the game's screen shows it (FBattleEffects::GroundColour), shade times lighter times as light at its middle, written to land on it by picture.to_land; where the game cannot say, the ground row's dust paint. The ring, the billows and the veil are not drawn there. Neither tall nor lumps (build 1758's lumps: lumps, lump_r, belly, crown_r, crown_up, wide, reach, smoke): all as before.
dry._low: Art director 08:03Z 20 November on build 1762's still from 60 m, a fifth of a second after the shot: the young lumps read as small pale balls. With low_s the dust is born low: until low_s.0 seconds old each lump and heap lies along the ground low_flat times as high as it is wide (as wide again as keeps its bulk), the way blast dust first skirts out, in its plain middle tone with no lit top and no shadow side, its dense part reaching only low_soft of the way out it will, so the young skirt has a soft edge. By low_s.1 seconds it has risen round, firmed and earned its light, so half a second after the shot it is the lump the art director passed in build 1762. The gun's smoke puffs, off the ground, keep their round shape and only firm and come into their light as late. shade is now six parts in a hundred either side of its middle, so each lump is of its own shade. No low_s: born round and lit, as in build 1762. Build 1764's stills from 60 m (09:28Z 20 November): the young skirt, soft-edged and in one flat tone a little under the ground's, was lost on the game's rippled sand, so nothing marked the shot for a third of a second. low_lit is the share of its light and shade a mound is born with: at 0.5 its top sits at about the ground's own tone (never the pale of a lit lump) and its foot is darker, so it reads as a low heap of dust; low_soft 1 gives it its firm edge from birth. No low_lit: 0, as in build 1764.

hot._how: Art director 07:08Z: close to the eye (within_m) a ground gun's flash, a machine gun's (Shots, mg) or a field gun's (Muzzle), is lit from within as the air guns' close flash: a yellow-white root at the muzzle (root to root_edge, its rim hot), an orange body (orange, its rim rim) with dense rims, shrinking rather than going see-through. Past within_m as before. Art director 13:54Z on the game's own frames (build 1720), where that read as a sticker: with tongues here, the close flash is instead a small white-yellow root right at the muzzle (root), melting into yellow, then the orange body, widest a third of the way out, which breaks into 3 to 5 ragged tongues with red only at their ends (red), and 2 to 4 short licks thrown sideways; its length is rolled between long x its usual length every round (mg_flame_m for a machine gun, 1.4 x flame_m for a gun), so no two match. Dense inside, its edge a pixel or two soft. glow: a thin glow glow_m past the flame, that opaque at dusk and glow_day_share of it by day. over: how far past white the root burns (see picture.lit_gain). wide: half its width, as a share of its usual length. Art director 16:30Z on build 1732's stills (root cream at 235,231,216, orange 230,152,4 with no blue: candy): these colours are WRITTEN values, aimed through the game's curve (picture._how). root at over 4 lands 253,250,234, luma 249, over a spot 5 to 9 px across on a 1600 still. orange lands about 234,141,41 (her 235,140,40; written 235,140,40 it landed 234,150,0). yellow_over: how far past white the yellow burns (1.175, as it did when over was 1.5; absent, a share of over). halo: a soft card of the root's colour round the root, that opaque at its inner edge and nothing halo_m further out, in place of the game's bloom (never over 0.25; 0 or absent: none). At 0.08 and 0.028 m it lifts the picture a quarter of the way to the root at most, 3 to 4.5 px out on a 1600 still. Art director 18:05Z on build 1746's stills (root 252,249,233, white for about 5 px along the bore, the glow down to the ground by about 8 px on a 1600 still): the game's own bloom already gives the glow, so the card is dropped (halo 0; halo_m kept for the day it is wanted again).

ground_cases._how: The grit up close (art director): within within_m of the eye, a ground machine gun (Shots with weapon mg) drops its spent brass out of the bottom of its receiver every round (as the war's machine guns did), falling with a little scatter to build a small heap under and beside the gun where the gunner lies; a towed or field gun (Muzzle at_gun, howitzer) opens its breech after_s after each shot and throws its big brass case out behind, where it lies for minutes, so the cases pile up behind the gun through a fight. A tank's cases stay inside it. Each case is a brass tube lit as metal (art director 07:08Z): a bright band toward the sun with a glint (glint, shine), a shade side and underside (shade), the dark open mouth (mouth) at one end when it is turned to the eye, and a soft contact shadow on the ground once it lies there (contact_shadow). Past most_lying cases lying at once, a new one lies only a moment. Each gun's cases use their own dice, so its rounds, strikes and smoke fall as they always did; a recipe without ground_cases draws none. They are left out when the screen is past three fifths full.

mg._note: art director 07:08Z: out of the bottom of the receiver (the MG 34 and 42, the Bren, the DP, the Browning, the Vickers), rifle-calibre cases about 6 cm; they lie long enough to heap up

bullet_strike._how: Art director 21:16Z: small dust spurts where a burst's rounds strike the ground (Shots, given the ground). About three rounds in ten kick one (pre-check 21:34Z: at one in two a firing gun cost about 16 puffs): a quick upward spurt and a low puff in the ground's dust colour, gone in under a second, scattered about the aim point by spread_mil of the range.

tracer._how: Brian 2026-11-18: 'i want tracer fire shown as well. 1 out of every 5 bullets with yellow'. As a belt was loaded: every fifth round of a gun is a tracer; the four between are not seen. Out of step between guns.
tracer._most: Art director 01:31Z: a near streak stays thin, no brighter than a far one, and is long on the screen for a frame or two (a whip, not a beam). A tracer is laid along its true heading, as wide on the screen from end to end, and no wider than most_px in the middle of the screen (times day_width by day: 7.5 px; a far one is 4.5; up to a sixth wider toward the edges, as the picture draws everything there). 0 takes the limit off. Passing a few metres off it drew 20 px and more before.

ricochet._note: a tracer striking the ground or armour sometimes skips up at an angle: a real sight in films and footage

tracer.render_note: airshow.py TRACER: radiance (0.15, 0.133, 0.0) at puff strength, as built for the air clips
tracer._day_solid: Art director 13:54Z on the game's own frames (build 1720), where a day tracer was a faint hairline 25 luma over pale ground: by day a tracer is a solid pale core (day_core, day_core_px across, day_over past white: see picture.lit_gain) inside a warm edge (day_edge), day_px across in all, straight-sided and at its whole opacity along its whole length. Pixels are drawn pixels: the art director's 3 and 5 px on a 1600 frame are 2 and 3.4 where the game draws 1072 across. At dusk as before. Art director 16:30Z (build 1732, core 231,226,212): day_core and day_over are written values aimed through the game's curve (picture._how); 255,241,151 at 2.72 times white lands 249,247,222 on a flat patch, and a core this thin measures some 5 to 13 lower, so on her 245,240,210.
tracer._day: Art director 21:07Z: by day only, the streak is 1.5 times wider and its pale core pushed toward 245,240,210, so a stream holds against a pale sky. Day is read from the hour's light (white by day); at dusk the streak is as ruled. One in five and 213,199,104 stay.
tracer._whole_path_s: Art director 02:13Z (build 1710): the close shot's whole path is a whip, one frame and gone, never a standing line. Shown for whole_path_s, under one frame at 60 a second; a frame is never missed. Nothing of a tracer is drawn behind the muzzle (or behind a ricochet's strike), and a whole path stops at its strike.
tracer._close: Art director 21:16Z (build 1690, a machine gun seen from 19 m showed no tracer line): below whole_path_below_m a tracer crosses in a frame or two, so its whole path is drawn at once, muzzle to strike, fading toward the muzzle (three lengths at 35, 68 and 100 per cent), for at least one frame.

mg_smoke._how: Art director 13:54Z: close to the eye (muzzle.hot.within_m), a machine gun's burst of 3 rounds or more leaves a thin wisp, a little paler and cooler than the ground (art director 14:26Z: a faint veil on pale and dark ground alike) at the muzzle, one puff every every_rounds rounds, living life_s and drifting on the wind; on dry ground (dust.vehicles.by_ground) with the muzzle under dust_under_m up, also a low puff of the ground's own dust kicked up just in front of it. alpha: the most the whole wisp is ever opaque, never over 0.25. Art director 16:30Z (build 1732, where the wisp lifted Idaho's pale ground by 6 luma and was not seen): colour 228,232,238, and the wisp reaches the full 0.25 where its puffs overlap. puff_share: one puff's opacity as a share of alpha (0.55 before, and absent). At 0.63 the overlaps peak at 0.25 (measured over 100 rounds; 0.75 passed it, 0.30).

picture._how: The game's picture (CampaignCameraPawn.cpp: Unreal's film curve, saturation 1.07, contrast 1.08, warm highlights, film toe 0.6) holds plain white (255) down to about 226, darkens and warms the darks (grey 60 shows as 31) and takes the blue out of a strong orange. tools/battle-fx/game_curve.py is that road in numbers: `lands` says what a written colour shows as in the game, `write` what to write to land on a number. lit_gain: the game's material multiplies every colour by this (the wrapper sets M_Highlight's Brightness to it) and the kit writes every colour that much darker, so all looks as before; but the hottest lights (muzzle.hot.over, tracer.day_over) are written up to that much past white. 1 or absent: nothing changes. air_guns._how: Brian 2026-11-18 19:35Z: 'make the gun fire very realistic and the tracer fire too'. Guns on aircraft (AirGun, called every frame while a trigger is down). A round flies at muzzle_mps plus the aircraft's speed, slows (drag, a share of its speed lost a second) and falls (drop). Every round flickers at the muzzle; one in tracer_every is the ruled tracer (tracer.colour, tracer.streak_m), burning for tracer_s. tracers._white: The core burns white-hot (as far past white as the picture allows, picture.lit_gain) within white_within_m of the eye and its nation's own colour from white_beyond_m on: near white at close range, as ruled.
tracers._px: body_px and core_px are the glow's and the core's width by day in the pixels the scene tells the kit. tracers._one_fan: A gun farther than one_fan_beyond_m from the eye fires tracers of one piece (see one_fan_px): its core was a pixel wide there, and a tracer costs half as much. Without the key every tracer is glow and core.

air_hit._how: Rounds striking an aircraft (AirHit, at the point hit, carried with that aircraft): a hot spit on the skin with two or three short tongues, sparks thrown off and slowed by the air so they fall away behind, a scrap or two of skin tumbling off (some bare metal catching the light), and a small dark puff left hanging where the hit was. air_hit._art_director_0440: Art director 04:40Z: a hit's puff hangs 3 to 4 s (smoke_s), growing to smoke_r1 times the strike size; from the strategy camera the spit on the skin is never under least_px 2 px on its flash frame, so far off a hit reads as a twinkle.

sparkle._how: A rifle-calibre or heavy machine gun round striking an aircraft (art director 15:02Z 20 November, air-fates-look D): a bright sparkle of one or two frames and nothing more, no puff and no scraps. points of them within within_s, the first where the round struck and the rest scatter_m about it on the skin, each size_m across for a .50 (by the gun's strike_m), alight life_s, burning over times past white, never under least_px on the screen (the pixels the scene tells the kit). burst._how: A 20 mm shell striking an aircraft (the same ruling; a row of air_guns with cannon 1): the small flash as before, sparks of them, fragments scraps of skin, and one black-grey puff puff_m across hanging puff_s where the hit was, a ragged roundish ball of a main puff and puff_lobes smaller ones crowding it (art director 19:52Z: one rough puff read as a bird or a moth). With this row; without it a cannon's hit is as it was.

air_trails._how: A trail from a moving point on an aircraft (TrailStart, TrailMove every frame, TrailStop). Puffs are laid every spacing_m along the path, each drawn smear x spacing longer behind it so they join in one line, and left hanging in the air (carried: the share of the aircraft's speed they keep) to drift with the wind. Each frame the young end is drawn from the point back to the newest puff, so a trail starts at the engine. A trail comes to full over ramp_s, darkening from colour to colour_full over darken_s; each puff widens from r0_m to r1_m as it hangs for life_s (grow: below 1 widens early, above 1 late) and pales toward colour_old. lumpy (0 to 1) makes some puffs bigger lumps and the rest smaller and shorter lived, and the smear shrinks over smear_s, so an old trail breaks into uneven lumps; rise_mps lifts the smoke. Fire adds ragged tongues streaming back about flame_m from the root, and its smoke starts at the flame's tips.

smoke._what: a damaged engine: thin and dark at the engine, widening (about three times by 2 s) and breaking into paler lumps

fire._what: an engine or tank on fire: ragged flame streaming aft from the root, black smoke rising from its tips

glycol._what: a holed radiator: a thin white vapour that soon thins out

air_trails._engine_out: Art director 15:38Z 20 November (air-fates-look G1) for Brian's 'if a engine is out there should be a lot more dark smoke strains from that engine and directly behind it on the tail': a dead engine always smokes. tail_wide_m: how wide the smoke is as it passes the tail, tail_m behind its source; the aircraft's own wake spreads it that fast, and the row's r1_m and widen_by_s widen it on after. fire: 1.5 m at the nacelle, 5 to 6 m past the tail, the densest black. oil (out and windmilling): 1.2 to 1.5 m and 4 to 5 m, dark grey, 0.6 to 0.7 opaque at the nacelle, lumpy, one torn column, a gout gout_wide times as wide and gout_alpha times as dense for gout_s every gout_every_s as the oil spits; wisps: the share of its pieces that throw a shred off its edge. streak (the fire put out, the airscrew feathered): 0.8 to 1 m and about 3 m, 0.3 to 0.4 opaque at the nacelle paling to 0.15 by 60 m behind; it never clears while the caller keeps it. doused: the extinguisher's white-grey puff for for_s, the flames of a burning trail shrinking back to the nacelle over flame_shrink_s, then the streak on its own (then_streak), grey at first and darkening. glycol: thinning to fade_to of itself over fade_over_s, then the streak. funnel._what: a ship's funnel smoke (the art director's ruling of 05:30Z 21 November, art-director/explosions/funnel-smoke-ruling.md): round puffs laid by time into the air the ship steams through, never the air trail's strips
funnel._how: TrailStart(Now, Id, At, her velocity, "funnel", the funnel's width at its top in metres) and TrailMove every frame with her velocity and, last, the share of her top speed she is making (0 to 1; left out, her speed over top_speed_mps). A puff keeps none of her speed: it drifts with the world's wind and climbs, its height rise_k x root(funnel) x age^(2/3) / cube root(felt wind), so a fast ship's plume lies low and a stopped one's stands up (felt wind never under felt_least_mps). A puff is lip_of_funnel funnel widths across at the lip and widens by wide_k x funnel^wide_by_funnel x (metres of felt wind gone by)^(2/3). One is laid every 1/overlap of a puff's width. even (the art director, 14:13Z 21 November: no sky between the puffs): every other puff goes each time the plume has doubled its width, so the ones left always stand evenly; a puff thins as the plume deepens in them (the same smoke over more of them), and over the last even share of each such stretch the ones that go thin to nothing while those between take their smoke up. The first even_near halvings come at each doubling, the next even_far sooner (each when the plume is even_step times wider: far astern it is faint and needs fewer puffs deep), the rest at each doubling again. Without even: as they widen only as many hang on as still overlap that deep, by an even spread. size, shade: each puff that much bigger or smaller, lighter or darker; rough its lumpy rim, and heart_round 1 keeps its heart ring a true round under that rim, so the outline billows and the middle of the plume stays even. The plume rolls: a slow wave along it, one value every roll_run puffs at the lip and twice as far apart each time the plume has doubled its width, so a roll is always about as long as the plume is wide; where the wave is high the puffs ride roll_lift of their radius higher and are roll_shade darker, where it is low as much the other way (no lift at the lip, in full by three lip widths; never more than that, no dice). A wide funnel's puffs are laid closer: overlap_wide deep at wide_funnel_m across and wider, between funnel_m and that in proportion, each holding as much less smoke. full is the look at full_from of her power and over, cruise the look at cruise_to and under, blended between: alpha a puff's opacity at the lip, fallen by e at fade_s seconds old (as the power fade_pow of its age: over 1 it holds while young, then goes sooner); age_s how long the oldest hang; colour at the lip going to colour_old by old_by_s. surge: when her power rises by rise within about within_s she rings up, and for for_s the smoke is the surge look. shadow_of_lit, shadow_k: a puff's side away from the sun. lip_least_px: a far ship's puffs are never under that many pixels at the lip (at most lip_most times their size), so her plume is fewer, bigger puffs; and where the lip is far_px.0 pixels or under they overlap only overlap_far deep, each as much denser (in full from far_px.1). life_s is only the row's mark as a trail of its own.

fuel._what: a fuel tank alight, the flamer: long torn flame streaming back past the tail into dense black smoke

mist._what: fuel spraying from a torn wing root: a white mist torn back and gone in a second or two (it often catches: TrailStart again as fuel or fire)

air_debris._how: A falling aircraft's debris row (AirFall once as the fall starts with its span and the deck height, AirFallMove every frame, AirFallStop when the model is gone). explode sheds fighter or bomber pieces at once (bomber at bomber_span_m or more), thrown throw_mps out and carried on at carry of its speed, with a short torn fireball; burn sheds burn_sheds over its fall, every_s apart, from first_s; spin sheds spin_sheds, the first a wing at wing_odds. A skin plate (plate_m across, painted face paint, bare metal inside bare) tumbles plate_tumble radians a second, so seen edge-on it thins and flutters, and glints when the sun catches it (glint, glint_power); it slows to sink at plate_sink_mps and drifts with the wind. A heavy piece (heavy_share of an explosion's, heavy_m, heavy_colour) drops at heavy_sink_mps. A wing (wing_chord_of_span) tumbles slowly down at wing_sink_mps.
